chunks: And from him, from Humayd ibn al-Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from al-Hasan ibn Hashim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: "And a woman who fears from her husband disobedience or aversion."

He said: "This is when the husband finds the wife displeasing and desires to divorce her, so she says to him: 'Retain me and do not divorce me, and I will leave for you what is on my back (dowry), and give you from my wealth, and make permissible for you my day and night (intimacy), so that becomes pleasing to him.'"

key_terms.إِعْرَاضاً: Aversion or turning away by the husband
key_terms.نُشُوزاً: Disobedience or deviation by the wife

ai.seo_question: What is the practical scenario of Khul' when a husband wants to divorce his wife due to displeasure?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the practical application of *Khul'* by illustrating a scenario where a wife, facing her husband's displeasure (*Nushuz* or *I'rad*), negotiates her release by offering financial compensation or intimacy. It highlights the consensual nature of *Khul'* in Shia jurisprudence, where the wife initiates the separation to avoid discord, aligning with the verse's allowance for mutual agreement in divorce. The narration underscores the flexibility in the form of compensation, whether material or relational, provided it pleases the husband.
